original_value: AbstractSpatially and temporally adaptive algorithms can substantially improve the computational efficiency of many numerical schemes in computational mechanics and physics‐based animation. Recently, a crucial need for temporal adaptivity in the Material Point Method (MPM) is emerging due to the potentially substantial variation of material stiffness and velocities in multi‐material scenes. In this work, we propose a novel temporally adaptive symplectic Euler scheme for MPM with regional time stepping (RTS), where different time steps are used in different regions. We design a time stepping scheduler operating at the granularity of small blocks to maintain a natural consistency with the hybrid particle/grid nature of MPM. Our method utilizes the Sparse Paged Grid (SPGrid) data structure and simultaneously offers high efficiency and notable ease of implementation with a practical multi‐threaded particle‐grid transfer strategy. We demonstrate the efficacy of our asynchronous MPM method on various examples including elastic objects, granular media, and fluids.

result.paraphrase: Abstractly, spatially and temporally adaptive algorithms can greatly boost the computational efficiency of many numerical schemes used in computational mechanics and physics-based animation. Recently, the Material Point Method (MPM) has shown a growing need for temporal adaptivity because material stiffness and velocities can vary substantially in multi-material scenes. In this work, we present a new temporally adaptive symplectic Euler scheme for MPM with regional time stepping (RTS), in which different regions use different time steps. We develop a time-stepping scheduler at the granularity of small blocks to preserve natural consistency with MPM’s hybrid particle/grid structure. The method leverages the Sparse Paged Grid (SPGrid) data structure and provides both high efficiency and notable ease of implementation through a practical multi-threaded particle-grid transfer strategy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our asynchronous MPM method on a range of examples, including elastic objects, granular media, and fluids.
